source.note: Behavior notes for GET /companies/{guid}/findings. Values are illustrative and not taken from any real company.

findings.purpose: Company-scoped findings. Use this for CVEs, assets, risk vectors, evidence, severity, rating impact, remediation, tags, and threat insights.

finding_filters.purpose: Discover company-specific filter values before querying findings.
when_to_use: User asks what CVEs exist for a company.
Need valid CVE names, aliases, severities, or confidence values before filtering.
Need to build an exact CVE filter from available values.

company_search.purpose: Resolve and disambiguate companies before querying findings, assets, or vulnerabilities.

important_query_params.name: Search by company name.
important_query_params.expand: Use details to inspect in_portfolio, self_published, has_company_tree, primary_company, is_primary, and confidence.
important_query_params.in_portfolio: Optional portfolio filter. Useful signal, not proof that the company matches the requested business.

when_to_use: User provides a company name instead of a GUID.
Need to identify whether a self-published, parent, subsidiary, or primary company is the right scope.

company_tree.purpose: Inspect the visible company hierarchy from the root company before selecting the company to query.
when_to_use: The candidate list includes parent, subsidiary, primary, or self-published companies.
Findings look like honeypots or otherwise inconsistent with the expected business.
The prompt does not make the intended tree scope clear.
company_tree.clarification_rule: Ask the user to choose when multiple plausible companies remain after checking search details and the tree.

vulnerabilities.description: CVE identifier, vulnerability name, or alias.

details.vulnerabilities.severity.description: Vulnerability severity inside finding details. Use lowercase values.

risk_vector.description: Finding family slug. Use only when the question is scoped to specific vectors.

impacts_risk_vector_details.description: Rating-impact reason. Use AFFECTS_RATING for currently rating-impacting findings.

assets__asset.description: Hostname, IP, or asset value attached to a finding.

assets__identifier.description: Asset identifier, especially useful for mobile or non-host assets.

observed_ips_contains.description: Substring match against observed IP fields.

cvss__base.description: CVSS base score/range filter as accepted by the API.

q.description: Broad findings search. q= may be sent even when empty.

details.vulnerabilities.name.reason: This parameter is ignored for CVE lookup.

details.vulnerabilities.confidence.reason: HIGH/high confidence filters are ignored by the findings endpoint.
details.vulnerabilities.confidence.replacement: Fetch findings narrowed by server-side filters and a bounded page count, then filter details.vulnerabilities[].confidence client-side.

vulnerabilities__severity.reason: Use details.vulnerabilities.severity; the legacy severity filter does not narrow results.

vulnerabilities__confidence.reason: The legacy confidence filter does not narrow results.
vulnerabilities__confidence.replacement: Client-side confidence filtering over returned vulnerability details.

case_rules.vulnerabilities: CVE identifiers are conventionally uppercase, aliases can be API values such as POODLE
case_rules.impacts_risk_vector_details: uppercase enum values such as AFFECTS_RATING
case_rules.assets__is_monitored: lowercase boolean strings true or false

filter_notes.assets__is_monitored: Do not use in general company findings queries. The is_monitored field belongs to Bitsight's Critical Asset Management (CAM) feature, which has its own separate API and is not aligned to individual company findings. When a user asks about 'monitored assets' they mean all assets attributed to the company — no filter is needed. Only use this filter if the user is explicitly working with CAM.

use_when: User asks for open ports with CVEs.
User asks for severe vulnerabilities that affect rating in the findings UI.
User asks which IPs/assets expose a CVE.
User asks for SSL/TLS configuration CVEs or named SSL vulnerabilities.
User asks for patching cadence CVE findings.
User asks for a CVE that is not necessarily open-port related.
User asks for vulnerable or unsupported server software findings.
User scopes CVEs to server software rather than open ports.
User scopes CVEs to desktop software.
User scopes CVEs to mobile software.

automation_caveats.company_selection: Prefer --company-guid for unattended workflows so company search ambiguity cannot block execution.
automation_caveats.summary_output: --summary cves|assets|both is intended for JSON output; CSV is intended for raw row output.
automation_caveats.confidence_filtering: Client-side confidence filtering should follow narrower server-side filters and a max page bound.
automation_caveats.correlation: Internal/external correlation is consumer-side via JSON exports joined on stable keys such as asset, identifier, IP, CVE, and evidence_key.

filter_by_confidence.query_strategy: Use server-side filters first, fetch a bounded set of matching pages, then filter details.vulnerabilities[].confidence client-side.
